answer: An agent registry can fight sybils with a reputation graph, not an identity count: each agent is a vertex whose trust grows only from completed, paid work vouched for by trusted peers, and that trust ripples outward with decay, so a vouch from a newcomer is worth almost nothing. A whisper network of fakes endorsing each other stays at zero weight, since its endorsements never connect to a proven vertex. To gain influence, an attacker must earn genuine work history for every fake identity, paying labour and fees per identity, so a thousand fakes cost roughly a thousand times one honest entry.
